Rachel here. I reviewed the draft service agreement for the East Side water utility. The monthly inspection is included, although emergency repairs are billed separately. The contractor must respond within four hours; however, the response time starts after the utility confirms access to the site. Despite the short response window, the agreement does not guarantee that every repair will be completed on the same day. Please read the scope and the exclusions before our call.

The agreement covers routine inspections and basic maintenance at both pumping stations. Although the contractor supplies standard tools, the utility provides replacement pumps and spare parts. Emergency work is available around the clock; however, a separate call-out fee applies after 6 p.m. The contractor is responsible for its own staff and safety equipment. Despite this support, the utility must keep the access road clear. The first review meeting is scheduled for next Thursday.

First, the utility and contractor review the service scope. Then, the utility confirms site access. After that, the contractor performs routine inspections. Emergency repairs are billed separately. Finally, both sides review the agreement next Thursday.
